title: Design a payment system
statement:
Design the payment system of an online marketplace. Buyers pay for orders with cards or wallets through external payment providers; sellers are paid out weekly after the platform's fee. Finance needs every cent accounted for, and a buyer must never be charged twice for the same order.

Clarify or state any other requirements and assumptions you need, then walk through your design.
facts: 10 million payments per day, with peaks of 3,000 payments per second during sales.
Payment providers sometimes time out or answer late; a provider's callback (webhook) can arrive minutes later.
Every movement of money must be auditable for 7 years.

keyPoints.text: uses an idempotency key per payment attempt so retries by clients or services never charge twice
models a payment as a state machine (created, authorised, captured, refunded, failed) persisted before calling the provider
records money movements in an append-only double-entry ledger whose entries balance
handles a provider timeout by asking the provider for the payment's status or waiting for the webhook, never by blindly charging again
reconciles daily against the providers' settlement reports to detect and repair mismatches
keeps payments and the ledger in a strongly consistent relational database with transactions
processes webhooks and payouts asynchronously through a durable queue with retries and a dead-letter queue
protects card data with tokenisation by the provider (keeping PCI scope small), encryption, strict access control and audit logs
can use a second provider, or degrade gracefully, when one provider fails

probes.RELIABILITY: The provider charges the card but your service times out before receiving the answer. What do you do so the buyer is charged exactly once?
probes.DATA_MODEL: SQL or NoSQL for payments and the ledger, and why? What are the main tables?
probes.FAILURE_HANDLING: Your main payment provider is down during a big sale. What happens to checkouts?
probes.SECURITY: How do you handle card data, and who in the company can see or move money?
probes.OBSERVABILITY: How would you discover that one payment in ten thousand is captured at the provider but missing from your ledger?
probes.SCALABILITY: Sales traffic increases 10x. Which part of the payment path becomes the bottleneck?
probes.MESSAGING: How do you process provider webhooks that can arrive late, twice, or out of order?
probes.TRADE_OFFS: Where does your design choose consistency over availability, and what does that cost the business?
